title: Hazel and the Protocol
premise: Sable Zhou, the last caretaker of Meridian Station's seed-vault garden, discovers the colony was abandoned decades ago and their transmissions to Earth have been looping into silence. When a distress signal arrives in a dead trade-tongue, Sable decodes it as a forged plea from a fleet that no longer exists — a lie someone built to keep two rival armadas from colliding over the colony's ruins. To sustain the deception, Sable must impersonate the dead colony's voice, aided by Idris Okonkwo, a defector navigator who teaches them the extinct language and, slowly, how to be loved. As the fleets converge and the forgery unravels, Sable chooses truth over duty: they broadcast the real record of the colony's death, forcing both fleets to confront what they were about to destroy. The book ends with the fleets standing down, the garden seeded with new life, and Sable and Idris choosing each other over the protocols that made them.
about_author: Casper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former hydroponics engineer who spent six years on Antarctic research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who tend things nobody else remembers.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Establishes daily life tending the seed vault on near-empty Meridian Station: watering rows meant for colonists who never arrived. Sable records an audio log admitting, almost jokingly, that no one will ever hear it. Emotional beat: tender loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Loop Number Four Thousand
chapters.summary: Sable discovers the station's outgoing reports have been auto-looping for years; Earth stopped listening long ago. Flashback fragments reveal the evacuation Sable refused to join. Beat: quiet horror breaking through denial.

chapters.title: A Voice in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Keshari, a trade language extinct two centuries. Sable can't read it but recognizes its rhythm from childhood lullabies. Beat: wonder piercing isolation.

chapters.title: The Defector at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Idris Okonkwo arrives claiming to have answered the signal — he's a navigator who deserted the Vossan fleet to decode it. Wary first meeting in the greenhouse. Beat: mutual suspicion with sparks of recognition.

chapters.title: What the Signal Says
chapters.summary: Idris translates: the signal is a forged plea for aid, apparently sent by Meridian itself, designed to stall two rival fleets heading for the system. Someone manufactured hope. Beat: dawning scale of the conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Forger's Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Together they trace the signal to a dead relay and find its author: Dr. Amara Chen, the colony's former director, who died keeping the lie alive. Her logs become their instruction manual. Beat: grief for a stranger who becomes family in memory.

chapters.title: Lessons in Extinction
chapters.summary: Idris begins teaching Sable Keshari so they can maintain the deception. Lessons in the garden double as intimacy; Sable's first spoken Keshari sentence is 'I am still here.' Beat: falling in love through language.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Scopes show the Vossan and Halcyon armadas slowing at the system's edge, held apart only by the signal's promise of survivors needing rescue. POV alternates via intercepted fleet chatter. Beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: The Lie Needs a Face
chapters.summary: Fleets demand direct communication with 'Meridian Command.' Sable must voice the dead colony live. First broadcast under Chen's identity; Idris feeds them lines. Beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming someone else.

chapters.title: Found Family, Fabricated
chapters.summary: Sable invents crew members to populate the fiction — names drawn from the garden's seed labels. The imaginary colony starts feeling real; Sable mourns people who never existed. Beat: bittersweet invention as love.

chapters.title: Halcyon Sends a Ship
chapters.summary: A Halcyon shuttle requests landing to 'assist survivors.' Sable and Idris scramble to stage a living station using drones, recordings, and light tricks. Beat: farce tightening into dread.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Halcyon officer Wren Adeyemi tours the station; Sable, masked and gloved, plays Chen's deputy. Wren notices the garden's impossible freshness. She leaves unconvinced but says nothing — yet. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Protocol
chapters.summary: Vossan intelligence flags linguistic anachronisms in Sable's broadcasts. Idris realizes his own defection may have been anticipated; his old commander sends a personal summons. Beat: paranoia corroding trust.

chapters.title: What Idris Is Running From
chapters.summary: Idris confesses: he helped design the original protocol that abandoned Meridian, and answering the signal was his penance. Sable's anger and forgiveness in the seed vault. Beat: the relationship's darkest hour and repair.

chapters.title: Wren Returns Alone
chapters.summary: Officer Adeyemi comes back off-duty, having decoded enough to know the truth. Instead of reporting it, she asks why. Sable shows her the garden and the real death records. Beat: an enemy becomes a co-conspirator; found family widens.

chapters.title: The Fleets Move
chapters.summary: Vossan command, tired of waiting, accelerates toward the planet; Halcyon matches the maneuver. The signal's stalling power expires in seventy-two hours. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Amara's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Decoding Chen's final log, they learn she intended all along for someone to eventually tell the truth — the lie was scaffolding, not the building. Sable decides to end the deception on their own terms. Beat: resolve crystallizing.

chapters.title: Broadcast: The True Record
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Sable hijacks the relay and broadcasts the colony's actual history — the abandonment, the deaths, the garden — in Keshari and plain speech, dropping the mask entirely. Both fleets go silent. Beat: devastating courage.

chapters.title: Standoff Over Ruins
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Fleet commanders demand explanations; Wren testifies to what she saw; Idris surrenders himself to vouch for the record's authenticity. The two armadas hang motionless above a graveyard. Beat: maximum stakes, everything risked.

chapters.title: What Duty Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: the fleets negotiate a joint memorial charter instead of territorial claim, seeded by Chen's protocol reworked into truth. Idris faces tribunal; Sable waits. Beat: justice tempered by mercy.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Idris returns, sentence commuted to service rebuilding Meridian as a shared research station. Colonists from both fleets arrive — the garden finally has its people. Sable plants the last seed row. Beat: earned hope, found family realized.

chapters.title: I Am Still Here
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Sable records one final log, signed with their own name this time, addressed to whoever comes next. Idris joins mid-recording; the last line is spoken together in Keshari. Beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty fulfilled.
